subject: Math
prompt: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse has length $20$ and one of the acute angles measures $30^°$. What is the length of the side adjacent to the $30^°$ angle?
explanation: In a right triangle, $\cos(\theta) = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$. With $\theta = 30^\circ$ and hypotenuse $= 20$, we have $\cos(30^\circ) = \frac{x}{20}$ where $x$ is the adjacent side. Since $\cos(30^\circ) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, we get $x = 20 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 10\sqrt{3}$.
